newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo head quits in Swedish industrial shake-up.
newsitem.headline: Volvo head quits in Swedish industrial shake-up.

text.p: Swedish corporate life was rocked Monday by a major shake-out in which the boss of vehicle maker Volvo quit and was replaced by the dynamic head of appliance maker Electrolux.

Soren Gyll's decision to quit came as something of a shock, although he had indicated earlier he would retire before too long after five years at the helm of the car, truck and bus maker. He was forced to deny reports last year that he was at odds with company Chairman Bert-Olof Svanholm.
Leif Johansson, the 45-year-old head of Electrolux, takes over at Volvo, leaving the empire of the Wallenberg family, the powerful business dynasty that holds a major chunk of Electrolux.

Johansson will be replaced by Michael Treschow as president and chief executive. Treschow is presently president and chief executive of construction and mining equipment company Atlas Copco, another firm in the Wallenberg sphere of influence.
Italian Giulio Mazzalupi, a senior Atlas Copco executive, becomes the first non-Swedish chief executive of the construction company, Atlas Copco said.

Svanholm said Gyll would remain on the board of Volvo. Gyll took over Volvo in the wreckage of a failed marraige with French carmaker Renault, selling off most non-core assets to concentrate on the tough world of making cars and trucks.
Analysts said Gyll's role was seen as having been fulfilled and said a dynamic figure was needed to boost Volvo's flat sales in international markets.

"He led a very successful disposal programme but that programme has been largely finished," said analyst Keith Hayes of Goldman Sachs. "It is a logical time for him to go with least disruption to the company."
Volvo said Gyll informed the board that he wished to leave his executive position at the annual general meeting of the company on April 23.
Gyll expressed willingness to remain on the board and Svanholm backed this proposal.
"The fact that Gyll is staying on the board means that people will not assume any change in strategy," analyst John Lawson of Salomon Bros told Reuters.
Gyll said in a statement that Volvo's goal of becoming exclusively a transport equipment group had essentially been implemented and that the group was strong, both financially and in its products.
"The group now faces a number of important strategic and structural decisions that will have consequences extending far into the future and whose implementation will demand continuity," Gyll said.
"It is against this background and since I had, in any event, intended to relinquish my executive duties next year at age 58, that I consider this is the proper time to pass the baton."
His successor, Johansson, joined Electrolux in 1984 and has been president since 1991 and chief executive officer since 1994, the statement said.
